title: Hilbert States for Decision-Making under Partial Observability
abstract: arXiv:2611.20970v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decision-making under partial observability can be fundamentally limited by information, even with known dynamics: distinct physical states can induce the same observation history while favoring different actions. We study three questions: when is full-state optimality unattainable, what information exactly preserves the best observation-based decision, and how does finite-data learning affect reliability? First, we characterize decision ambiguity through conditional action preferences. We give a zero-regret criterion, a positive lower bound for conflicting uniquely optimal actions on positive-probability regions with uniformly positive cost gaps, and an exact binary-action regret formula. This also shows why physical-state ambiguity alone need not cause decision loss. translated_title: 部分可观测决策的希尔伯特状态
translated_abstract: 摘要：部分可观测条件下的决策可能在根本上受制于信息，即使系统动态已知也是如此：不同的物理状态可能产生相同的观测历史，却偏好不同的动作。我们研究三个问题：何时全状态最优性无法实现，什么信息恰好能保留基于观测的最佳决策，以及有限数据学习如何影响可靠性？首先，我们通过条件动作偏好来刻画决策歧义性。我们给出了一个零遗憾准则、对于正概率区域上具有一致正成本差距的冲突唯一最优动作的正下界，以及一个精确的二元动作遗憾公式。这也说明了为什么仅有物理状态歧义不一定会导致决策损失。其次，对于平面上的两个动作和平方终端目标成本，我们推导出了条件期望成本差异的精确内积表示，使用了三个……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出用希尔伯特状态刻画部分可观测下的决策歧义性，给出了零遗憾准则与二元动作遗憾的精确公式，并揭示了何种信息恰好能保留基于观测的最优决策。
en_tdlr: This paper uses Hilbert states to characterize decision ambiguity under partial observability, providing a zero-regret criterion, an exact binary-action regret formula, and identifying the information that preserves optimal observation-based decisions.
